Maintenance Report — MNT-0179-005

Asset: WELL-0179 (NE-08 Well 179, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 02 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 02 Jun 2023 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 13 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0179-0033 on 2023-06-01 Report written: 03 Jun 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0179-0033 at 10:15 on 2023-06-01 found crude oil on the pad: about 3.8% of the pad area, estimated 1.1 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.3 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 194 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 155 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.3 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0179-005 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.2% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0179-016

Asset: WELL-0179 (NE-08 Well 179, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 29 Sep 2024 08:00 · Finished: 01 Oct 2024 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 55 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0179-0102 on 2024-09-26 Report written: 03 Oct 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0179-0102 showed the wellhead at 29.5 °C with the air at 25.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 8 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.
